story.title: Volcanic Eruption Disrupts Flights at Indonesia's Main Airport
story.summary: An eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau has led to the suspension of flights at Jakarta's main airport and five other airports in Indonesia. The eruption caused ash to spread, resulting in the cancellation of over 500 flight movements and affecting thousands of passengers. Additionally, school activities and fishing operations have also been halted due to safety concerns.

explore_lenses.label: Why did ash ground flights so widely?
explore_lenses.title: Ash clouds crossed major air corridors
explore_lenses.summary: The disruption was driven by ash at flight altitudes over western Indonesia, not simply by the volcano’s proximity to Jakarta. Aviation and meteorological authorities used formal hazard notices to close or restrict airports as conditions changed.

claims.text: BMKG identified two ash-cloud clusters on September 6: one up to 20,000 feet over areas including Jakarta, Banten and West Java, and another up to 50,000 feet spreading westward over Banten, Lampung, Bengkulu, the Sunda Strait and the Indian Ocean.
Airport closures were coordinated by airport authorities with BMKG, AirNav Indonesia, airport operators and other agencies through NOTAMs, SIGMETs and volcanic-ash advisories.
AirAsia said volcanic ash poses a significant threat to aircraft operating near volcanic clouds and cancelled or rescheduled all of its Jakarta flights during the closure.

Airport closures were coordinated by airport authorities with BMKG, AirNav Indonesia, airport operators and other agencies through NOTAMs, SIGMETs and volcanic-ash advisories.
AirAsia said volcanic ash poses a significant threat to aircraft operating near volcanic clouds and cancelled or rescheduled all of its Jakarta flights during the closure.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Airport operating status remained changeable because it depended on ash dispersion, airspace conditions and safety assessments.

explore_lenses.label: How did the eruption reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A long eruptive episode followed months of alert
explore_lenses.summary: The September 6 disruption followed elevated activity that officials say began in July, then intensified into a roughly 25-hour continuous eruptive episode beginning late September 4.

claims.text: Indonesia’s Geological Agency says Anak Krakatau has been at Level III (Siaga, or Alert) since July 2, 2026, after eruptions resumed following a lengthy lull.
PVMBG recorded continuous eruption-related seismic activity from 23:07 WIB on September 4 until 00:04 WIB on September 6, followed by a 30-second Strombolian eruption at 03:53 WIB.

The Geological Agency reported that activity had intensified since July and described the September 6 eruption as the strongest in that period; it linked repeated eruptions to continued magma and gas supply beneath the volcano.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for nearby communities?
explore_lenses.title: Monitoring, distance limits and remote schooling
explore_lenses.summary: Officials kept the volcano at Level III and focused on ash exposure, crater-area hazards and fast-changing flight conditions. Authorities reported no detected tsunami anomaly as of the morning of September 6, but advised coastal residents to follow official updates.

claims.text: PVMBG kept Anak Krakatau at Level III and warned that follow-on eruptions remained highly possible; it cited risks from hot-rock ejection, heavy ashfall and possible lava flows, and maintained a 3-kilometer exclusion zone around the active center.
BMKG’s 20 tsunami gauges and its HF radar showed no sea-level anomaly as of 07:00 WIB on September 6; BMKG assessed tsunami probability at that time as low, below 40%.

Lampung ordered schools to switch from in-person classes to online learning on September 7-8, saying the measure was to protect students and education workers from ash exposure; the province said learning itself was not being stopped.

story_report.summary: Mount Anak Krakatau erupted, disrupting aviation across Indonesia as more than 500 flights were canceled at Jakarta and five other airports. The ash-related disruption also suspended school activities and fishing, affecting travelers and communities in areas exposed to the volcano’s fallout. Authorities continued to monitor conditions as airport operations and other restrictions depended on safety assessments.

sections.heading: Ash Clouds Disrupt Indonesian Airspace
sections.body: Indonesia’s meteorology agency identified two ash-cloud clusters on September 6. One reached 20,000 feet over areas including Jakarta, Banten and West Java, while another rose to 50,000 feet and spread westward over Banten, Lampung, Bengkulu, the Sunda Strait and the Indian Ocean. Airport closures were coordinated through aviation notices and volcanic-ash advisories involving BMKG, AirNav Indonesia, airport operators and other agencies.

sections.heading: Anak Krakatau Activity Remains Elevated
sections.body: Indonesia’s Geological Agency has kept Anak Krakatau at Level III alert since July 2, after eruptions resumed following a lengthy lull. PVMBG recorded continuous eruption-related seismic activity from late September 4 until shortly after midnight on September 6, followed by a 30-second Strombolian eruption. The agency said activity had intensified since July and described the September 6 event as the strongest of that period, linking repeated eruptions to continued magma and gas supply beneath the volcano.

sections.heading: Officials Maintain Volcano Safety Measures
sections.body: PVMBG said follow-on eruptions remained highly possible, citing risks including hot-rock ejection, heavy ashfall and possible lava flows, while maintaining a 3-kilometer exclusion zone around the active center. BMKG reported no sea-level anomaly by 07:00 WIB on September 6 and assessed tsunami probability then as low, below 40%. In Lampung, schools were ordered to use online learning on September 7-8 to limit ash exposure, while officials said education would continue.

unresolved.text: Officials cannot determine from current activity whether a larger eruption will occur.
The duration of aviation restrictions, school measures and fishing disruptions remained dependent on continued ash and volcano monitoring.

related_stories.title: Egyptian TV Presenter Sarah Khalifa Sentenced to Death in Drug Trafficking Case
related_stories.summary: Sarah Khalifa, a prominent Egyptian TV presenter known for her program 'Mission Impossible', has been sentenced to death by a Cairo court. She was convicted along with 11 others for their involvement in a drug trafficking ring, which included manufacturing and distributing narcotics.

related_stories.title: Israeli Strikes on Southern Lebanon Result in Multiple Casualties
related_stories.summary: Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon have reportedly killed four people, including two women, and injured at least 20 others, according to the Lebanese health ministry. The strikes were described as a response to an alleged drone attack by Hezbollah targeting Israeli troops in the region. The Israeli military stated that the operation aimed to target Hezbollah infrastructure following the attempted attack.
